added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no base gate log, so the added-failure count was not taken

findings.text: follow-on: the test docstrings (here and project_state.py:1951) say the refusal is EROFS, but a chmod'd tree yields EACCES (Errno 13) as the negative-control log shows, so the done_when's literal 'raises EROFS' is not reproduced, only the equivalent refusal; the wording could be corrected or a genuinely read-only tree used.

follow-on: the journal root and glob are written twice -- _pending_transaction_journals (:1953-1956) and recover_project_state_transactions (:1962,:1966); recovery could call the helper so a future journal name added to one cannot be silently skipped by the read-path guard.

follow-on: the guard lists journals outside the lock and recovery re-lists only when entered, so a journal created between the listing and the recovery call is not recovered on this read; it is self-healing (the journal persists for the next read) and the move path holds resource locks, so this is non-blocking.

item_verdicts.goal: the node's goal is that the project-state read path takes no write lock when nothing needs recovering; reckon/project_state.py:466 guards the recovery call on _pending_transaction_journals(docs_dir) (project_state.py:1946), so a journal-free read opens no lock file and creates none.

justifications.durability: tests/test_a_read_takes_no_lock.py:121 asserts the recovery lock is absent after a journal-free writable read and reddens when the guard is removed (reproduced: 2 failed EXIT=1), while :148 asserts a present journal is still recovered, so both the skip and the recover directions are guarded and the marker is created by the code rather than passed in.
justifications.evidence: the done_when names tests/test_a_read_takes_no_lock.py, the manifest records 3 passed EXIT=0 and the negative control 2 failed EXIT=1, and I independently reproduced both at 8c4f4c60a (head 3 passed EXIT=0; guard removed 2 failed, 1 passed, EXIT=1) in scratch trees under $TMPDIR, though the refusal there is EACCES on a chmod'd tree, not the EROFS the done-when's wording names.
justifications.fit: reckon/project_state.py:1946 names the helper by what it does, reuses the module's existing Path and lock idioms, and the commit carries a conventional subject with a body and no attribution or plan label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: reckon/project_state.py:466 calls recover_project_state_transactions only when _pending_transaction_journals(docs_dir) (project_state.py:1946) is non-empty, and read_resource is the only production caller of recovery (grep over reckon/ finds no other), so the whole read path is covered.
justifications.reuse: no capability is forked -- recovery keeps its own locking and the change adds only a lock-free listing -- but the journal root and glob are written twice (project_state.py:1953-1956 and :1962,:1966) rather than shared, so the two could drift.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the diff -- reckon/project_state.py, tests/test_a_read_takes_no_lock.py and the evidence fragment -- is inside the reviewed manifest's declared write paths, and the code change is two hunks of +13 lines.
